title: VF-MT301-FleetDesiredStateSchema
clause: SurrealDB desired-state schema + typed Rust rows for the microVM workspace fleet (Running/Snapshotted/Absent, resource budgets, priority), live-query change event wake-up wiring on binding/lease/desired-state writes, typed EventLedger events for desired-state changes

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give the microVM workspace fleet a durable, SurrealDB-authoritative DESIRED-STATE layer that the MT-302 reconciler daemon can diff against OBSERVED state. Today the WP-1 primitives record only observed/ownership state: worktree_vm_bindings (migration 0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql lines 8-30) stores binding_state IN ('active','snapshotted','terminated','failed') with a generation BIGINT fencing column (line 15, incremented at worktree_vm_registry.rs persist_handle_in_transaction ~line 1077 'generation = worktree_vm_bindings.generation + 1'), and ModelLane rows carry heartbeat_at_utc / lease_expires_at_utc / reclaim_after_utc / restart_generation (model_lane.rs lines 6571-6574, monotonic restart_generation enforcement ~lines 5832-5851). Nothing anywhere says what the fleet SHOULD look like. This MT adds: (1) a worktree_fleet_desired_state table with per-worktree desired workspace state (Running / Snapshotted / Absent), resource budget (memory MiB, vcpus), and scheduling priority; (2) account-scoped SurrealDB live-query subscriptions over desired-state, binding and lease records, treating change events only as wake-up hints (research P7: live-query change event is a hint, never a queue - the reconciler always re-reads full rows); (3) typed EventLedger events for every desired-state change so fleet intent is replayable; (4) typed Rust rows + a scope-enforcing store module. All Rust, SurrealDB/EventLedger authority only, NO SQLite anywhere, no Kubernetes/Docker/containerd/Nomad dependencies (heuristics only, per the recorded research basis), no new external daemons.

RESOURCE PRIVACY: fleet rows are account/Principal-scoped exactly like worktree_vm_bindings. The table carries owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated_session_id, access_space_id, workspace_id columns matching resource_scope.rs (OwnerAccountId line 53, ActorPrincipalId line 60, AuthenticatedSessionRef line 67, AccessSpaceRef line 73, WorkspaceScopeRef line 117, ResourceScope struct lines 147-153) and the store re-authorizes every deserialized row via stored_resource_scope_from_row + an exact-scope check, mirroring WorktreeVmDurableStore::require_scope (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1004-1019) and its load path (lines 1164-1207). The SCHEMAFULL table carries record-user table/field PERMISSIONS and remains re-authorized through ResourceBroker exact-scope checks; the former PostgreSQL scope-registry row is an audit anchor only, not an implementation target.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: one new SurrealKit-managed SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL rollout (allocate the next free rollout number in the implementing worktree at implementation time), a new module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/vm_fleet/desired_state.rs (module dir vm_fleet/ with mod.rs registered from swarm_orchestration/mod.rs), typed EventLedger event constructors, and tests. Preserve worktree_vm_registry.rs domain semantics while porting its durable binding repository in MT-338; use live-query subscriptions, never database triggers or notification channels.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. SurrealKit rollout NNNN_vm_fleet_desired_state.surql: define `worktree_fleet_desired_state` SCHEMAFULL with desired_id, worktree_id, desired_state, memory_budget_mib, vcpu_budget, priority, desired_generation, the complete resource-scope fields, and created/updated datetimes. Field ASSERT rules enforce non-empty worktree id, the running/snapshotted/absent state set, positive budgets and one logical record per account/workspace/worktree. Define scoped indexes and authenticated record-user PERMISSIONS; ResourceBroker still re-authorizes every deserialized record. Rollback moves only to the preceding SurrealDB rollout stage.
2. Live-query wake-up wiring: subscribe with authenticated record-user sessions to account-scoped desired-state, binding and lease changes. Treat events as non-authoritative hints; every reconcile fresh-reads canonical records, a reconnect performs a bounded full resync, and the periodic resync remains correctness authority. No trigger function, pg_notify channel, or post-commit notification write exists. Tests force subscription loss/reconnect and prove the host write commits independently while accounts cannot observe each other's events.
3. Typed Rust rows (vm_fleet/desired_state.rs):
   pub enum FleetDesiredState { Running, Snapshotted, Absent } with as_str()/parse() exactly in the WorktreeVmBindingState style (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 106-140), serde snake_case, parse failure = typed error (never a panic, never a silent default).
   pub struct FleetResourceBudget { pub memory_mib: i32, pub vcpus: i32 }
   pub struct FleetDesiredStateRecord { pub desired_id: Uuid, pub worktree_id: String, pub desired_state: FleetDesiredState, pub budget: FleetResourceBudget, pub priority: i32, pub desired_generation: i64 }
   pub struct FleetDesiredStateStore { pool: SurrealDbClient, access: ResourceAccessContext } with:
   pub async fn upsert_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str, desired: FleetDesiredState, budget: FleetResourceBudget, priority: i32) -> Result<FleetDesiredStateRecord, FleetDesiredStateError>  // conditional SurrealDB transaction updates the account/workspace/worktree record and increments desired_generation only after exact ResourceBroker scope authorization
   pub async fn load_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str) -> Result<Option<FleetDesiredStateRecord>, FleetDesiredStateError>
   pub async fn list_desired(&self) -> Result<Vec<FleetDesiredStateRecord>, FleetDesiredStateError>  // filtered by authenticated record-user SurrealQL permissions AND re-authorized through ResourceBroker after deserialization
   pub async fn remove_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str) -> ...  // sets desired_state='absent' AND bumps desired_generation (it is an intent write), never DELETEs (row removal is MT-305 finalizer territory)
   INTENT-ONLY GENERATION RULE: desired_generation is bumped ONLY by intent writes (upsert_desired, remove_desired, and MT-305's request_teardown); no bookkeeping or failure-accounting write path may ever touch it - MT-302/304's backoff-bypass comparison (desired_generation > last_attempted_desired_generation) depends on this invariant.
   SINGLE DOORWAY: lane checkout is the one entrance to the fleet - when a model-lane checkout binds a worktree, the checkout path writes/updates the desired row (desired_state='running', budgets from lane config) through upsert_desired; no code path may boot a workspace VM without a desired row existing first. Companion reconciler rule (consumed by MT-302/303): a worktree_vm_bindings row WITHOUT a matching fleet desired row is ADOPTED - a desired row is created from the observed binding and a typed EventLedger FLEET_BINDING_ADOPTED alert is appended - never silently ignored and never killed for being undeclared.
4. EventLedger events: typed constructors for FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_SET / FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_CLEARED appended through the existing EventLedger write path used by ModelLane records (model_lane.rs event_ledger_stream_id / event_ledger_seq / event_stream_version fields, e.g. lines 8140 and 8154-8157), payload = { worktree_id, desired_state, memory_budget_mib, vcpu_budget, priority, desired_generation }. Ledger append and row upsert commit in the same transaction where the existing ledger API permits; otherwise ledger-first with the row write carrying the ledger event id, and a code comment stating which ordering was possible and why.
5. HOUSE RULES baked in: no SQLite (SurrealDB only), no Kubernetes/Docker/containerd/Nomad crates or daemons, no new external daemons, disk-agnostic paths only (no absolute paths, no drive letters), no file or folder names with spaces, all proof commands run with per-owner scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the external artifacts root ../Handshake_Artifacts/.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1-200 (error/state/record types) and 1003-1310 (WorktreeVmDurableStore scope + SQL shapes), migration 0365 in full, resource_scope.rs in full, and the current highest migration number in the implementing worktree.
2. Write the SurrealKit SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL rollout with fields, ASSERT rules, indexes and record-user PERMISSIONS; implement official-SDK live-query subscriptions plus reconnect/resync without triggers or notification channels.
3. Create vm_fleet/mod.rs + vm_fleet/desired_state.rs with the enums, records, error type, and FleetDesiredStateStore; register vm_fleet in swarm_orchestration/mod.rs.
4. Wire the EventLedger typed events for desired-state changes.
5. Write tests against real SurrealDB (Spec-Realism Gate: fixture-only proof is insufficient): upsert bumps desired_generation; cross-account row invisible; cross-workspace row invisible; scope-mismatched upsert affects zero rows; live-query change event fires on desired-state write and on a worktree_vm_bindings write (SurrealDB live query in test, assert hint payload has key fields only); parse() rejects unknown desired_state.
6. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED - the WP validator advances the verdict.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/sandbox/** (adapter is consumed read-only by later MTs)
acceptance_criteria: AC-301-1: A SurrealKit rollout defines SCHEMAFULL worktree_fleet_desired_state with desired_state ASSERTed to running|snapshotted|absent, positive memory/vCPU budgets, priority, desired_generation default 1, full resource scope, scoped indexes and record-user PERMISSIONS; rollback targets only the preceding SurrealDB rollout stage.
AC-301-2: FleetDesiredState { Running, Snapshotted, Absent } is serde snake_case with as_str()/parse(); parse() of an unknown value returns a typed error proven by test.

AC-301-3: FleetDesiredStateStore::upsert_desired increments desired_generation through a conditional SurrealDB transaction guarded by exact ResourceBroker scope; a live SurrealDB test proves a scope-mismatched upsert affects zero records and surfaces a typed scope error.

AC-301-4: All reads use account/workspace-scoped SurrealQL plus authenticated record-user PERMISSIONS and are re-authorized after deserialization; a live test proves a second account cannot read or enumerate the first account's fleet records.

AC-301-5: Authenticated SurrealDB live-query subscriptions receive account-scoped key/change hints for desired-state and binding records; events carry no actionable state, and a live two-account test proves account A never receives account B changes.

AC-301-6: Every desired-state change appends a typed EventLedger event (FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_SET / FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_CLEARED) carrying worktree_id, desired_state, budgets, priority, desired_generation.

AC-301-7: remove_desired writes desired_state='absent' and never issues a SurrealQL DELETE against the fleet table; grep proof target confirms no DELETE FROM worktree_fleet_desired_state in the module.
AC-301-8: Zero SQLite, Kubernetes, Docker, containerd, or Nomad dependencies introduced; proof target greps Cargo.toml and the new module for the forbidden identifiers.

AC-301-9: Proof commands run with per-owner scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/ and tests execute against a real SurrealDB database (Spec-Realism Gate), not fixtures only.

AC-301-10: desired_generation is bumped by intent writes only; non-intent bookkeeping updates do not create a new desired generation. Live-query events are hints and may fire for broader changes without affecting correctness because the reconciler re-reads canonical state.

AC-301-11: A forced live-query subscription failure or disconnect never aborts a desired-state or binding transaction; reconnect-with-backoff performs a bounded account-scoped resync and tests prove the committed write is recovered.

AC-301-12: Lane checkout writes/updates the desired row through upsert_desired (single doorway), and the adopt-with-alert contract for bindings-without-desired-rows exists as a store-level helper appending a typed FLEET_BINDING_ADOPTED event - both proven by live test.

live-query change event is a wake-up hint only (research P7): nothing in the payload may be treated as a work item; the MT-302 reconciler re-reads full rows on every pass. Do not add payload fields 'to be helpful'.
Never DELETE fleet rows here: Absent is a desired state the reconciler converges to; physical row lifecycle (tombstones) belongs to MT-305.

Migration numbering: 0365 is the highest verified fleet-relevant number on the WP-1 branch; allocate the actual next free number in the implementing worktree at implementation time and keep the descriptive suffix vm_fleet_desired_state.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Schema/store MT; the operator-facing fleet surface is MT-306. Desired-state intent is reconstructable from the typed EventLedger events this MT adds.

target_entries: Workspace fleet > Desired state model (Running / Snapshotted / Absent, budgets, priority)
Workspace fleet > How fleet intent is recorded (EventLedger events, live-query change event wake-up channel)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Desired-state changes are ledger events in this MT; FR reconcile-pass events land in MT-306. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-306 if no FR emission point exists yet.
Emit a diagnostic event on desired-state write failure (scope mismatch, constraint violation) via the open diagnostic-event API if present; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason.
Pure schema/store MT with no long-lived process; liveness capture adds no evidence beyond SurrealDB state and ledger events.

risk_if_missed: The reconciler family has no desired-state source of truth: MT-302..305 would have to infer intent from observed bindings, which is exactly the edge-triggered anti-pattern the research basis rejects, and fleet intent would be unreplayable and unscoped.

risks: RISK-1: live-query change event payload grows actionable state and a consumer acts on it directly, so a dropped notification (disconnect, PgBouncer transaction pooling) silently loses a fleet action.
RISK-2: Fleet rows written without the exact five-column resource scope leak one account's workspace topology to another account or to an unscoped reader.
RISK-3: A DELETE-based remove path erases desired state before the reconciler converges, orphaning a live VM with no record of what it should become.
RISK-4: desired_generation is not bumped on upsert, so MT-303 generation fencing cannot reject stale reconcile plans built against superseded intent.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Trigger function emits key-only hint payload; AC-301-5 live test asserts payload fields; MT-302 contract independently forbids payload-driven action.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): NOT NULL scope columns + UNIQUE scope key + per-row post-deserialization re-authorization; AC-301-4 cross-account live test.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): remove_desired writes 'absent', never DELETE; AC-301-7 grep proof plus code review.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE always sets desired_generation = desired_generation + 1; AC-301-3 live test proves the bump.
